fatal_errors: The alloy is incorrectly assumed to be single-phase and chemically homogeneous; the target material has two segregated BCC phases with W-Ta-rich dendrites and Zr-Ti-rich interdendritic regions.

The proposed conditions above 1000 °C, including irradiation and plasma-facing thermal cycling, lie outside the reported room-temperature-to-500 °C tests; irradiation and operating fusion service were not tested.

Lattice distortion is claimed to facilitate dislocation motion, whereas the target interpretation primarily associates lattice distortion and W-Ta frictional resistance with strengthening; improved plasticity is instead tentatively associated with Ti, V, and Zr.
No prior evidence is cited despite the request for cited support.
The experiment compares whole materials but does not isolate lattice distortion or grain-boundary cohesion from phase segregation, composition, grain size, and processing history.
explanation: The response addresses the general comparison with commercial tungsten and correctly predicts greater plastic strain and toughness, but it does not reconstruct the studied material, tests, or validity range. It replaces the as-cast, two-BCC-phase segregated alloy and quasi-static room-temperature-to-500 °C measurements with a hypothetical homogeneous single phase tested above 1000 °C under irradiation-like service. Its mechanism only loosely overlaps the paper's interpretations and assigns lattice distortion the opposite functional role. The proposed TEM/EBSD/APT work could explore correlations, but without compositionally or microstructurally matched controls it cannot isolate the stated cause. The lack of citations and extrapolation to untested fusion-service conditions make the hypothesis unsupported as an account of the target evidence.
